commits.summary: Compare 30 Spring changes at public APIs (verification pending)
commits.body:
Register 94 questions and run each caller on the specified parent and landing in a fresh JVM. All 31 intended contrasts and 30 unchanged controls held. Preserve the three merged counterexamples in YAML, mail copying and protobuf JSON Lines, the partially committed SQL script, the lost JDBC descriptor, and independent database readback at Mono completion. Examples 478–507 check 23 module build pairs and all compiled classes in seven pinned historical slices.

All 30 example validators with replay and all 55 selected suites passed. Five earlier campaign audits stayed byte-identical. Negative checks reject swapped historical class bytes, companions, YAML adapters and a client compiled on the wrong revision. Independent jobs 20261126-131411-replay-94-spring-predictions-across-30-p and 20261126-131422-trace-spring-mail-copies-and-r2dbc-loan repeat the complete comparison and 24 debugger trials at two original methods.

commits.summary: Recheck Spring findings on published releases (verification pending)
commits.body:
The original callers reproduce the three merged counterexamples and a misleading Jupiter diagnostic on published Spring 7.1.0. All 46 outcomes on the seven historical release pairs agree with their pinned class slices. Spring 5.3.18 also reproduces the three original listener histories. Record the 5.1.4 to 5.1.5 JDBC binary break and prepare the upstream reproductions. The P29 maintainer follow-up adds Javadoc and gives the same instructions and six matching JVM histories.

All 62 published-release observations passed a side-specific check against the original results. Deliberately changed outcomes, bytecode hashes, classpath order and version were rejected. All six selected suites passed and the older Spring release check still agrees. The independent 188-history replay and 24 original-method debugger trials passed. Job 20261126-132138-replay-published-spring-versions-and-the repeats the 62 published histories and the cron follow-up offline and compares the three output files byte for byte.
